miniProject.title: An optimizer and numerics test bench
miniProject.brief: Add optim/ to numlab: gradient descent, heavy-ball and AdamW with clipping, schedules and restartable state; a KKT and proximal-gradient pair checked against a solver; and the stable reductions. Compare the optimizers on changed geometry against eigenvalue predictions, then diagnose one divergence and one finite-precision failure.
steps: Implement gradient descent, heavy-ball and AdamW with norm clipping (the exact projection), an update-indexed schedule and a state object holding parameters, moments, step count and schedule clock. Every loop exits with one status: residual converged, stagnated, non-finite or iteration cap, and a test forces each one.

Run all three on quadratics with condition numbers 10, 100 and 1000, once diagonal and once rotated by a random orthogonal matrix. Before running, predict the gradient-descent rate from the eigenvalues; report the full gradient norm and objective gap against gradient evaluations, and compare with the prediction.

Diagnose one divergence: take a step slightly above 2/L, project the iterates onto the eigenvectors and show that only the top mode grows, at the predicted factor |1 - eta L| per step. Then add minibatch noise to a finite-sum least-squares problem: check the with-replacement gradient covariance Sigma/B empirically and the constant-step plateau variance against eta sigma^2/(lambda(2 - eta lambda)) on a scalar model.

Feed a constant gradient g and check the moments against the finite geometric sums (1 - beta1^t) g and (1 - beta2^t) g^2. Then, on one deterministic quadratic, match torch.optim.AdamW in float64 on the same clipped gradients and per-step learning rates, as in the adaptive unit. Save the state halfway, resume and check the final state against an uninterrupted run within 1e-12, and use the unclipped full gradient as the stationarity residual.

Change the two-coordinate QP from the KKT unit, solve it by hand and with CVXPY and Clarabel, and record every KKT residual and the solver status. Derive soft thresholding, then run proximal gradient on a lasso with a non-identity A and step 1/||A||_2^2; check it against a closed form on a diagonal A and against CVXPY and the lasso optimality residual on the general A.

Build the reductions: a log-sum-exp for finite nonempty inputs, left-to-right, balanced and Kahan sums, and online mean and variance, tested on cancellation, large offsets and float16 storage with float32 accumulation against math.fsum and float64 oracles. Diagnose one finite-precision failure end to end, such as the float16 running sum that stalls or the one-pass variance that returns zero, and show the repair.
deliverables: numlab/optim/: the optimizers with exit statuses and restartable state, the KKT and proximal code, and the reductions.
The tests: rate predictions, the divergence projection, the noise checks, the AdamW oracle and resume, the KKT residual table, the lasso checks and the reduction oracles.
notes/optimization.md: the predictions beside the measurements and both failure diagnoses.

rubric.pass: Measured gradient-descent rates on all six quadratics are compared with the eigenvalue predictions.
rubric.strong: Rotation is shown not to change the gradient-descent rate, with the reason, and momentum's gain is reported per gradient evaluation.

rubric.pass: The divergent run is traced to the top eigenmode at the predicted factor, and the noise covariance and plateau match their formulas within Monte Carlo error.
rubric.strong: The stopping statuses separate the divergent, stagnated and converged runs without manual inspection.

rubric.pass: AdamW matches PyTorch within 1e-12 and resume equals the uninterrupted run.
rubric.strong: A test shows that restoring parameters without moments or the schedule clock changes the trajectory.

rubric.pass: The QP has every KKT residual and the solver status recorded, and the lasso passes its optimality residual.
rubric.strong: Residuals carry stated tolerances, and solver success is never accepted without them.

rubric.pass: Each reduction matches its oracle, and one finite-precision failure is diagnosed and repaired.
rubric.strong: The note separates precision lost in storage from precision lost in accumulation.

miniProject.feedsInto: Capstone component 5, optimizer stability: the comparison, the divergence diagnosis and the finite-precision failure.
